In summary, our research is concerned with
the translocation and metabolism of auxin in intact bean seedling.
the translocation of auxins from the site of application in intact bean seedling.
the regulation of the movement of auxin in intact plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

translocation of auxins in intact bean seedling is a complex process which is affected by several factors including auxin concentration, the nature of the auxin, and the physiological status of the plant.

the acropetal translocational pattern of auxin in intact plants is regulated by a complex of factors which are sensitive to concentration of the auxin, the nature of the auxin molecule, the age of the plant, and the physiological state of the plant.
the acropetal translocations of auxin are regulated by the auxin itself and the auxin antagonists, and the basipetal translocation of 3-indoleacetic acid is regulated by protein synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the acropetal translocatory patterns of auxin are influenced by several factors, including concentration, the presence of antiauxins, and the state of protein synthesis.

translocation of auxins is a complex process involving both xylem and the phloem, and is subject to regulation by the concentration of auxin in the translocating tissue, the presence of antiauxin, and the rate of auxin metabolism in the tissue.
translocation of 1.5 micrograms of auxin from a single injection point is regulated by a complex interaction of auxin, auxin antagonist, and inhibitor of protein synthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
auxin translocation is highly sensitive to concentration and that translocation to shoots and roots is regulated by different mechanisms.
the relative exchangeability between xylem- and phloem-borne auxin is an important factor regulating the distribution of auxin in intact plants.
auxin is a dynamic compound that is constantly moving in the plant.
